sentences.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，諱榮，太祖之養子，蓋聖穆皇后之侄也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Ruiwu Xiaowen, whose personal name was Rong, was the adopted son of Taizu and was in fact a nephew of Empress Shengmu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, posthumously known as Ruiwu Xiaowen, bore the personal name Rong. He was Taizu's adopted son and a nephew of Empress Shengmu.

sentences.zh: 本姓柴氏，父守禮，太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: His original surname was the Chai clan; his father was Shouli, who had retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was born into the Chai family. His father Shouli had retired from the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：柴翁者，嘗獨居室，人以為司冥事。

translations.literal: (The Longpingji states: There was an Old Man Chai who once lived alone in his room, and people thought he dealt with matters of the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Longpingji, an elder of the Chai clan once lived alone in his room, and people believed he had dealings with the realm of the dead.

sentences.zh: 一日，笑不止，妻問其故，不答。

translations.literal: One day he laughed without stopping; his wife asked the reason, but he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: One day he could not stop laughing. When his wife asked why, he refused to say.

sentences.zh: 翁嗜飲，妻醉之以酒，乃曰：「上帝有命，郭郎為天子。

translations.literal: The old man loved drink; his wife made him drunk with wine, and then he said: "Heaven has commanded that Master Guo shall become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The old man loved wine, so his wife plied him with drink until he blurted out: "Heaven has decreed that Master Guo shall become emperor."

sentences.zh: 」考柴翁即守禮之父，史佚其名。）〉

translations.literal: " Investigation shows that Old Man Chai was the father of Shouli; the history does not record his name.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " It is held that this Old Man Chai was Shouli's father, though the history does not give his name.)〉

sentences.zh: 帝以唐天祐十八年，歲在辛巳，九月二十四日丙午，生於邢州之別墅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, bingwu, in the eighteenth year of Tang Tianyou, the year xinsi, at a villa in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (bingwu) in Tianyou 18 of Tang (xinsi year), at a country estate in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 年未童冠，因侍聖穆皇后，在太祖左右。

translations.literal: Before he had reached the age of the capping ceremony, he attended Empress Shengmu and was at Taizu's side.
translations.idiomatic: While still a boy, he attended Empress Shengmu and remained close to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 時太祖無子，家道淪落，然以帝謹厚，故以庶事委之。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu had no son, and the family's fortunes had declined; yet because the Emperor was careful and sincere, Taizu entrusted him with household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had no sons of his own, and the household had fallen on hard times, but he found the boy conscientious and dependable and began entrusting him with day-to-day affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝悉心經度，資用獲濟，太祖甚憐之，乃養為己子。

translations.literal: The Emperor devoted himself to planning and management, and supplies were made adequate; Taizu cherished him greatly and therefore adopted him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: The boy managed everything with care, kept the household supplied, and won Taizu's deep affection; Taizu eventually adopted him as his son.

sentences.zh: 漢初，太祖以佐命功為樞密副使，帝始授左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Taizu was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs for his merit in assisting the founding, and the Emperor was first appointed General of the Left Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty Taizu became vice commissioner of military affairs for his founding service, and the future emperor received his first commission as general of the Left Gate Guards.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《國老談苑》云：周世宗在漢為諸衛將軍，嘗遊畿甸，謁縣令，忘其姓名，令方聚邑客蒱博，勿得見，世宗頗銜之。

translations.literal: (The Guolao tanyuan says: When Zhou Shizong was a general of the guards under Han, he once traveled in the capital region and called on a county magistrate, whose name is forgotten; the magistrate was just gathering local guests for gambling and would not receive him, and Shizong bore considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: (The Guolao tanyuan records that while serving as a guards general under Han, the future Zhou Shizong once toured the capital region and called on a county magistrate whose name is lost to us. The magistrate was hosting a gambling party for local guests and refused to see him, and Shizong never forgot the slight.

sentences.zh: 及即位，令因部夫犯贓數百匹，宰相範質以具獄上奏，世宗曰：「親民之官，贓狀狼籍，法當處死。

translations.literal: When he acceded to the throne, that magistrate, because laborers under his command had embezzled several hundred bolts of cloth, had the full case submitted by the chief minister Fan Zhi; Shizong said: "An official close to the people, with corruption so flagrant—by law he should be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, that same magistrate was implicated when laborers under his command embezzled hundreds of bolts of cloth. Chief minister Fan Zhi submitted the completed case. Shizong said, "An official charged with caring for the people, and his corruption this brazen—the law calls for death."

sentences.zh: 」質奏曰：「受所監臨財物有罪，上贓雖多，法不至死。

translations.literal: " Fan Zhi memorialized: "Taking property under one's supervision is a crime, but though the amount embezzled is large, the law does not reach death."
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhi replied, "Embezzling property under one's supervision is indeed a crime, but even with a large sum involved, the statute does not prescribe death."

sentences.zh: 」世宗怒，厲聲曰：「法者自古帝王之所制，本以防奸，朕立法殺贓吏，非酷刑也。

translations.literal: " Shizong grew angry and said in a stern voice: "Law is what emperors and kings have made since antiquity, originally to guard against wrongdoing; that I make law to kill corrupt officials is not cruel punishment."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong flared up and said sharply, "Law is what rulers have fashioned since antiquity to keep wrongdoing in check. When I use the law to execute corrupt officials, that is not cruelty."

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「陛下殺之則可，若付有司，臣不敢署敕。

translations.literal: " Fan Zhi said: "Your Majesty may kill him if you wish, but if the case is handed to the responsible offices, your servant dares not sign the edict."
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhi said, "Your Majesty may execute him if you insist, but if the case goes through the regular judiciary, I cannot sign the edict."

sentences.zh: 」遂貸其命。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon his life was spared.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " In the end his life was spared.)〉

sentences.zh: 二年，太祖鎮鄴，改天雄軍牙內都指揮使，領貴州刺史、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In year 2, when Taizu was stationed at Ye, he was changed to commander of the inner guard of the Tianxiong Army, and given charge of Guizhou as governor while serving as honorary Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Taizu took command at Ye, he was made commander of the Tianxiong Army's inner guard, given Guizhou as his prefecture, and granted the honorary title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，留帝守鄴城。

translations.literal: In winter of year 3, when Taizu entered the capital to quell the internal crisis, he left the Emperor to guard Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Taizu marched into the capital to settle the internal crisis and left him to hold Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年正月，太祖踐祚，帝懇求入覲，忽夢至河而不得渡，尋授澶州節度使、檢校太保，封太原郡侯。

translations.literal: In the first month of Guangshun year 1, when Taizu ascended the throne, the Emperor earnestly requested an audience; he suddenly dreamed of reaching a river but being unable to cross; shortly thereafter he was appointed military governor of Cangzhou and honorary Grand Mentor, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Guangshun 1, after Taizu took the throne, he pleaded for an audience in the capital. He dreamed of coming to a river he could not cross, and soon afterward was appointed Cangzhou military governor and honorary grand mentor, enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝在鎮，為政清肅，盜不犯境。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was at his post, his administration was clear and strict, and bandits did not violate the borders.
translations.idiomatic: At his post his rule was austere and orderly, and bandits did not dare cross his borders.

sentences.zh: 先是，澶之裏巷湫隘，公署毀圯，帝即廣其街肆，增其廨宇，吏民賴之。

translations.literal: Previously the lanes and alleys of Cang were cramped and damp, and the government offices were ruined; the Emperor at once widened the streets and markets and enlarged the official buildings, to the benefit of officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The town lanes had been cramped and the government offices dilapidated; he widened the streets and rebuilt the offices, to the lasting benefit of officials and people alike.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王贊傳》：周世宗鎮澶淵，每旬決囚，贊引律令，辨析中理。

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Wang Zan》 in the 《History of Song》: When Zhou Shizong was stationed at Cangyuan, he held trials of prisoners every ten days; Wang Zan cited statutes and ordinances and analyzed them with sound reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song biography of Wang Zan records that when Shizong governed Cangzhou he held criminal hearings every ten days. Wang Zan cited statutes and argued cases with such sound reasoning

sentences.zh: 問之，知其嘗事學問，即署右職。）〉

translations.literal: When questioned, it was learned that he had once pursued learning; he was immediately given a post on the right.)〉
translations.idiomatic: that Shizong asked about his background, learned he had studied the classics, and promptly gave him a senior appointment.)〉

sentences.zh: 二年正月，兗州慕容彥超反，帝累表請征行，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 2, Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou rebelled; the Emperor repeatedly memorialized requesting to go on campaign, and Taizu commended him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yanzhou. He memorialized again and again asking to take the field, and Taizu praised his zeal.

sentences.zh: 及曹英等東討，數月無功，太祖欲親征，召群臣議其事，宰臣馮道奏以方當盛夏，車駕不宜沖冒。

translations.literal: When Cao Ying and others campaigned eastward for several months without success, Taizu wished to campaign in person; he summoned the ministers to discuss the matter, and the chief minister Feng Dao memorialized that it was just midsummer and the imperial carriage should not brave the heat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Ying's eastern campaign dragged on for months without result, Taizu decided to lead the army himself. Feng Dao and the other chief ministers argued that midsummer was no season for the emperor to expose himself on campaign.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「寇不可玩。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "A foe must not be trifled with.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu replied, "You cannot take an enemy lightly.

sentences.zh: 如朕不可行，當使澶州兒子擊賊，方辦吾事。

translations.literal: If I cannot go myself, then send the boy from Cangzhou to strike the bandits—that will settle my affair."
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot go, send the lad from Cangzhou to smash the rebels—that will do the job."

sentences.zh: 」時樞密王峻意不欲帝將兵，故太祖親征。

translations.literal: " At that time Wang Jun of the Bureau of Military Affairs did not wish the Emperor to command troops, and therefore Taizu campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jun, the military affairs commissioner, did not want him in command, so Taizu took the field himself.

sentences.zh: 六月，兗州平。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yanzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou fell in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was given the additional titles of honorary Grand Tutor and Co-Manager of Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was promoted to honorary grand tutor and appointed co-manager of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝入覲。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 3 the Emperor came to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he came to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 三月，授開封尹兼功德使，封晉王。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed Mayor of Kaifeng and concurrently Merit Commissioner, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was named mayor of Kaifeng and merit commissioner and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 二月庚戌，潞州奏，河東劉崇與契丹大將軍楊袞，舉兵南指。

translations.literal: On gengxu in the second month, Luzhou reported that Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan grand general Yang Gun had raised troops and were pointing south.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the second month Luzhou reported that Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan general Yang Gun had mobilized and were marching south.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，宰臣馮道率百僚上表請御殿，凡三上，允之。

translations.literal: On renxu the chief minister Feng Dao led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial requesting that the Emperor hold court; they submitted three times, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Feng Dao led the full bureaucracy in three memorials asking the new emperor to hold formal court, and he consented.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以中書令馮道充山陵使，太常卿田敏充禮儀使，兵部尚書張昭充鹵簿使，御史中丞張煦充儀仗使，開封少尹、權判府事王敏充橋道使。

translations.literal: On dingmao Feng Dao, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was made commissioner for the imperial tomb; Tian Min, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made ritual commissioner; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, was made commissioner for the imperial regalia; Zhang Xu, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made commissioner for ceremonial arms; and Wang Min, Junior Mayor of Kaifeng and acting administrator of the prefecture, was made commissioner for bridges and roads.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Feng Dao was named tomb commissioner; Court of Sacrifices director Tian Min, ritual commissioner; Minister of War Zhang Zhao, regalia commissioner; Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xu, arms commissioner; and acting Kaifeng mayor Wang Min, bridges-and-roads commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河東賊將張暉率前鋒自團柏谷入寇，帝召群臣議親征。

translations.literal: The Hedong rebel general Zhang Hui led the vanguard in invasion through Tuanbai Valley; the Emperor summoned the ministers to discuss campaigning in person.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong rebel Zhang Hui led his vanguard through Tuanbai Valley. The emperor called the ministers together to debate a personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 宰臣馮道等奏，以劉崇自平陽奔遁之後，勢弱氣奪，未有復振之理，竊慮聲言自來，以誤於我，陛下纂嗣之初，先帝山陵有日，人心易搖，不宜輕舉，命將禦寇，深以為便。

translations.literal: The chief ministers Feng Dao and others memorialized that since Liu Chong had fled in panic from Pingyang, his strength was weak and his spirit broken, and there was no reason he could recover; they privately feared that reports had come of their own accord to mislead us; Your Majesty had just succeeded, the former emperor's tomb rites were imminent, hearts were easily unsettled, and a light move was inadvisable—it would be far better to commission generals to repel the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and the other chief ministers argued that since Liu Chong's rout at Pingyang his forces were spent and demoralized and unlikely to recover; they suspected the reports might be deliberate misinformation; the emperor had only just succeeded, Taizu's burial was near at hand, and morale was fragile—a rash move was unwise, and sending generals would be far safer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「劉崇幸我大喪，聞我新立，自謂良便，必發狂謀，謂天下可取，謂神器可圖，此際必來，斷無疑耳！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Liu Chong, taking advantage of our great mourning and hearing that I am newly enthroned, will think the moment favorable; he is sure to hatch a reckless scheme, thinking the realm can be taken and the imperial regalia seized—at this juncture he is certain to come; there is no doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Liu Chong will seize on our mourning and my fresh accession. He will think the moment perfect, hatch some mad scheme, and convince himself the realm and the throne are within his grasp. He will come now—of that I have no doubt!"

sentences.zh: 」馮道等以帝銳於親征，因固諍之。

translations.literal: " Feng Dao and the others, because the Emperor was keen on campaigning in person, therefore remonstrated firmly.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing how set he was on leading the army in person, Feng Dao and the others pressed their objections hard.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔唐太宗之創業，靡不親征，朕何憚焉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In former times Emperor Taizong of Tang in founding his enterprise never failed to campaign in person—why should I shrink from it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Emperor Taizong of Tang built his dynasty he led every campaign in person. Why should I hold back?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下未可便學太宗。

translations.literal: " Feng Dao said: "Your Majesty cannot yet simply imitate Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao replied, "Your Majesty is not yet in a position to imitate Taizong."

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「劉崇烏合之眾，茍遇王師，必如山壓卵耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said again: "Liu Chong's mob gathered in a day—if they meet the imperial army, it will surely be like a mountain crushing an egg."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor went on, "Liu Chong's rabble will scatter the moment they meet our army—it will be a mountain falling on an egg."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「不知陛下作得山否？

translations.literal: " Feng Dao said: "I do not know whether Your Majesty can play the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao said dryly, "I wonder whether Your Majesty can play the mountain."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took offense and ended the discussion.

sentences.zh: 詔諸道募山林亡命之徒有勇力者送於闕下，仍目之為強人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuits to recruit from the mountains and forests fugitives and outlaws with courage and strength and send them to the court, designating them as "strong men."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every circuit to recruit fugitives and outlaws from the hills who had proven strength and send them to the capital under the label "strong men."

sentences.zh: 帝以趫捷勇猛之士多出於群盜中，故令所在招納，有應命者，即貸其罪，以禁衛處之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because swift and fierce warriors mostly came from among bandit gangs, therefore ordered localities to recruit them; those who answered the call had their crimes pardoned and were placed in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He believed the fiercest fighters often came from the outlaw ranks, so he offered amnesty to volunteers and enrolled them in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 至有朝行殺奪，暮升軍籍，讎人遇之不敢仰視。

translations.literal: There were even cases of robbery and murder in the morning and enrollment in the army rolls by evening; enemies who encountered them did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Some men robbed and killed in the morning and wore imperial uniform by evening; their enemies would not dare meet their eyes.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦患之，其後頗有不獲宥者。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself was also troubled by this; afterward many were not granted pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself grew uneasy about the policy, and later many applicants were refused amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，潞州奏，河東劉崇入寇，兵馬監押穆令均部下兵士為賊軍所襲，官軍不利。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the third month Luzhou reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded; the troops under Mu Lingjun, army supervisor, had been struck by the rebel army, and the imperial forces had fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the third month Luzhou reported Liu Chong's invasion and a defeat: troops under army supervisor Mu Lingjun had been ambushed and the imperial force had taken heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 詔天雄軍節度使符彥卿領兵自磁州固鎮路赴潞州，以澶州節度使郭崇副之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong Army, to lead troops from Cizhou by the Guzhen route toward Luzhou, with Guo Chong, military governor of Cangzhou, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing of the Tianxiong Army was ordered to march from Cizhou by the Guzhen road toward Luzhou, with Cangzhou's Guo Chong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔河中節度使王彥超領兵取晉州路東向邀擊，以陜府節度使韓通為副。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Yanchao, military governor of Hezhong, to lead troops by the Jinzhou route eastward to intercept, with Han Tong, military governor of Shaanfu, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was to strike east along the Jinzou route to intercept the enemy, with Shaanfu's Han Tong as deputy.

sentences.zh: 命宣徽使向訓、馬軍都指揮使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使何徽、滑州節度使白重贊、鄭州防禦使史彥超、前耀州團練使符彥能等，領兵先赴澤州。

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; Fan Aineng, commander of the horse army; He Hui, commander of the foot army; Bai Chongzan, military governor of Huazhou; Shi Yanchao, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou; Fu Yanneng, former regimental trainer of Yaozhou; and others were ordered to lead troops first to Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, Fan Aineng, He Hui, Huazhou's Bai Chongzan, Zhengzhou's Shi Yanchao, former Yaozhou trainer Fu Yanneng, and others were sent ahead to Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，制：「大赦天下，常赦所不原者，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: On xinsi an ordinance: "A general amnesty is proclaimed for the realm; even those crimes not normally pardoned in regular amnesties are all forgiven and removed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he proclaimed: "A general amnesty for the realm—even crimes normally excluded from routine amnesties are forgiven.

sentences.zh: 諸貶降責授官，量與升陟敘用，應配流徒役人，並放逐便。

translations.literal: All officials demoted, degraded, or assigned by punishment shall, as appropriate, be promoted and re-employed in order; all those sentenced to exile, penal servitude, or forced labor are likewise released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted officials shall be considered for reinstatement; exiles and convicts shall be released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 諸道州府所欠去年夏秋租稅並放。

translations.literal: All summer and autumn land tax arrears owed by circuits, prefectures, and districts from the previous year are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding summer and autumn land taxes from the previous year are remitted in every circuit and prefecture.

sentences.zh: 內外見任、前文武職官並與加恩，父母在者並與恩澤，亡沒者與封贈，其母妻未敘者，特與敘封」云。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials currently in office or formerly serving, inside and outside the capital, shall receive added favor; those whose parents are living shall receive favor as well; the deceased shall receive posthumous titles and gifts; and where mothers and wives have not yet received titles, special grants of enfeoffment shall be made," it said.
translations.idiomatic: Serving and retired civil and military officials shall receive honors; living parents shall share in those honors, deceased parents shall receive posthumous titles, and mothers and wives not yet ennobled shall receive special grants of rank," the edict concluded.

sentences.zh: 前涇州節度使史匡懿卒。

translations.literal: Shi Kuangyi, former military governor of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jingzhou military governor Shi Kuangyi died.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以劉崇入寇，車駕取今月十一日親征。

translations.literal: On guiwei an edict, because Liu Chong had invaded, ordered that the imperial carriage set out on the eleventh day of this month for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, citing Liu Chong's invasion, he ordered the imperial army to take the field in person on the eleventh of the month.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以樞密使鄭仁誨為東京留守。

translations.literal: On jiashen Zheng Renhui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made resident defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen military affairs commissioner Zheng Renhui was left as defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，車駕發京師。

translations.literal: On yiyou the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the emperor left the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，至澤州。

translations.literal: On renchen he reached Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he reached Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，王師與河東劉崇、契丹楊袞大戰於高平，賊軍敗績。

translations.literal: On guisi the imperial army fought a great battle with Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Yang Gun at Gaoping, and the rebel army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the imperial army fought Liu Chong and the Khitan Yang Gun in a great battle at Gaoping and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕行次河陽，聞劉崇自潞而南，即倍程而進。

translations.literal: Initially, when the imperial carriage halted at Heyang and heard that Liu Chong was coming south from Lu, it immediately doubled the pace of advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the army paused at Heyang and learned that Liu Chong was marching south from Lu, the emperor ordered a forced march.

sentences.zh: 是月十八日至澤州，既晡，帝御戎服，觀兵於東北郊，距州十五里，夜宿於村舍。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of that month he reached Zezhou; after the hour of shen he donned battle dress and reviewed the troops in the northeastern suburbs, fifteen li from the prefecture, and lodged that night in a village house.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Zezhou on the eighteenth. That afternoon he put on armor, reviewed the troops fifteen li northeast of the city, and spent the night in a farmhouse.

sentences.zh: 十九日，先鋒與賊軍相遇，賊陣於高平縣南之高原。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth the vanguard met the rebel army; the rebels formed battle lines on the high ground south of Gaoping County.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth the vanguard met the enemy, who had drawn up on the heights south of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 有賊中來者，云：「劉崇自將騎三萬，並契丹萬餘騎，嚴陣以待官軍。

translations.literal: Someone came from among the rebels and said: "Liu Chong personally commands thirty thousand horsemen, together with more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen, drawn up in strict array awaiting the imperial army."
translations.idiomatic: A defector reported that Liu Chong commanded thirty thousand cavalry himself, reinforced by more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen, all drawn up in tight formation awaiting the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 」帝促兵以擊之，崇東西列陣，頗亦嚴整。

translations.literal: " The Emperor urged the troops forward to attack; Chong deployed his lines east and west, and they were also quite strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered an immediate attack. Liu Chong deployed his men in east-west lines, and their formation was formidable.

sentences.zh: 乃令侍衛馬步軍都虞候李重進、滑州節度使白重贊將左，居陣之西廂；

translations.literal: He then ordered Li Chongjin, chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot armies, and Bai Chongzan, military governor of Huazhou, to command the left wing, stationed in the western section of the battle line;
translations.idiomatic: He assigned Li Chongjin, chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot armies, and Huazhou's Bai Chongzan to the left wing on the west side of the line;

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使何徽將右，居陣之東廂；

translations.literal: Fan Aineng, commander of the palace horse army, and He Hui, commander of the palace foot army, to command the right wing, stationed in the eastern section of the battle line;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Aineng, commander of the palace cavalry, and He Hui, commander of the palace infantry, to the right wing on the east;

sentences.zh: 宣徽使向訓、鄭州防禦使史彥超，以精騎當其中；

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and Shi Yanchao, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, to take the center with elite cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun and Zhengzhou's Shi Yanchao to hold the center with elite cavalry;

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使張永德以禁兵衛蹕。

translations.literal: and Zhang Yongde, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, to guard the imperial procession with the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhang Yongde, commander of the Palace Front Division, to guard the emperor with the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 帝介馬觀戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor, in armor on horseback, watched the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched from horseback in full armor.

sentences.zh: 兩軍交鋒，未幾，樊愛能、何徽望賊而遁，東廂騎軍亂，步軍解甲投賊，帝乃自率親騎，臨陣督戰。

translations.literal: When the two armies clashed, before long Fan Aineng and He Hui fled at the sight of the rebels; the cavalry of the eastern wing fell into disorder, and the foot soldiers cast off their armor and went over to the enemy; the Emperor then personally led his elite cavalry to the front to direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the armies engaged, Fan Aineng and He Hui fled at the sight of the enemy. The eastern cavalry collapsed, and infantry threw down their arms and defected. The emperor then led his personal guard into the fight and took command on the front line.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·馬仁瑀傳》：從世宗親征劉崇，王師不利，仁瑀謂眾曰：「主辱臣死！

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Ma Renyu》 in the Longpingji: Following Shizong on the personal campaign against Liu Chong, when the imperial army fared badly, Renyu said to the troops: "When the lord is shamed, the minister must die!"
translations.idiomatic: (The Longpingji biography of Ma Renyu records that during Shizong's campaign against Liu Chong, when the imperial army faltered, Renyu cried to his men, "When the sovereign is disgraced, his servants must die!"

sentences.zh: 」因躍馬大呼，引弓連斃將卒數十，士氣始振。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he spurred his horse forward with a great shout, drew his bow, and in succession killed several dozen enemy officers and soldiers, and the troops' morale began to revive.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He spurred forward shouting, loosed his bow, and cut down dozens of enemy officers and men in succession until the army's spirit revived.)〉

sentences.zh: 今上馳騎於陣前，先犯其鋒，戰士皆奮命爭先，賊軍大敗。

translations.literal: The present sovereign galloped before the battle line and was first to strike their vanguard; the warriors all strove with their lives to take the lead, and the rebel army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor charged to the front and was first to strike the enemy vanguard. His soldiers fought with desperate courage, and the rebel army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 日暮，賊萬餘人阻澗而陣，會劉詞領兵至，與大軍迫之，賊軍又潰，臨陣斬賊大將張暉及偽樞密使王延嗣。

translations.literal: At dusk more than ten thousand rebels blocked a stream and formed lines; when Liu Ci arrived leading troops and joined the main army in pressing them, the rebel army collapsed again; the rebel grand general Zhang Hui and the false military affairs commissioner Wang Yansi were beheaded on the field.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk more than ten thousand rebels made a stand across a stream. Liu Ci arrived with reinforcements, and together with the main force they drove the enemy into a second rout, killing the rebel generals Zhang Hui and the pretender's military affairs commissioner Wang Yansi on the field.

sentences.zh: 諸將分兵追襲，僵屍棄甲填滿山谷。

translations.literal: The generals divided their forces in pursuit; corpses and discarded armor filled the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The generals split up in pursuit. Corpses and abandoned armor choked the valleys.

sentences.zh: 初夜，官軍至高平，降賊軍數千人，所獲輜重、兵器、駝馬、偽乘輿器服等不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In the first watch the imperial army reached Gaoping; several thousand rebel soldiers surrendered; the baggage, weapons, camels and horses, false imperial carriages, regalia, and garments captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: By first watch the imperial army had reached Gaoping. Several thousand enemy soldiers surrendered, and the captured baggage, arms, camels, horses, and counterfeit imperial regalia were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 其夕，殺降軍二千餘人，我軍之降敵者亦皆就戮。

translations.literal: That evening more than two thousand surrendered troops were killed, and those of our army who had gone over to the enemy were also all put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: That night more than two thousand prisoners were executed, and imperial soldiers who had defected to the enemy were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 初，兩軍之未整也，風自東北起，不便於我，及與賊軍相遇，風勢陡回，人情相悅。

translations.literal: At first, before the two armies had formed up, the wind rose from the northeast, unfavorable to us; when we met the rebel army, the wind suddenly shifted, and hearts were mutually gladdened.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies had fully deployed, a northeast wind blew against the imperial force. The moment they engaged, the wind swung around, and the soldiers took it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 戰之前夕，有大星如日，流行數丈，墜於賊營之上。

translations.literal: On the eve of battle a great star bright as the sun streaked several zhang and fell upon the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle a great star bright as the sun streaked across the sky for many yards and fell on the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 及戰，北人望見官軍之上，有雲氣如龍虎之狀，則天之助順，亶其然乎！

translations.literal: During the battle the northerners saw above the imperial army cloud vapors shaped like dragons and tigers—was Heaven's aid to the righteous not indeed so!
translations.idiomatic: During the fight the northerners saw dragon- and tiger-shaped clouds above the imperial army. Heaven's favor for the righteous cause could hardly have been clearer.

sentences.zh: 是日，危急之勢頃刻莫保，賴帝英武果敢，親臨寇敵，不然則社稷幾若綴旒矣。

translations.literal: That day the perilous situation could not have been preserved for a moment; it was thanks to the Emperor's heroic courage and resolution in personally facing the foe that the altars of state were not nearly as a dangling tassel.
translations.idiomatic: That day the battle hung by a thread for moments on end. Only the emperor's courage in facing the enemy in person saved the dynasty from near collapse.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝宿於野次。

translations.literal: That evening the Emperor lodged in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: That night he camped in the open field.

sentences.zh: 甲午，次高平縣。

translations.literal: On jiawu he halted at Gaoping County.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he halted at Gaoping County.

sentences.zh: 詔賜河東降軍二千餘人各絹二匹，並給其衣裝，鄉兵各給絹一匹，放還本部。

translations.literal: An edict granted each of the more than two thousand surrendered Hedong troops two bolts of silk and also provided their clothing; local militia each received one bolt of silk and were released to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each of the more than two thousand surrendered Hedong troops given two bolts of silk plus clothing, and each local militiaman one bolt, then sent them home.

sentences.zh: 是日大雨。

translations.literal: That day there was heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell that day.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕至潞州。

translations.literal: On wuxu the imperial carriage reached Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor reached Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 河南府上言，前青州節度使常思卒。

translations.literal: Henan Circuit reported that Chang Si, former military governor of Qingzhou, had died.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Circuit reported the death of former Qingzhou military governor Chang Si.

sentences.zh: 己亥，侍衛馬軍都指揮使、夔州節度使樊愛能，侍衛步軍都指揮使、壽州節度使何徽等並諸將校七十餘人，並伏誅。

translations.literal: On jihai Fan Aineng, commander of the palace horse army and military governor of Kuizhou; He Hui, commander of the palace foot army and military governor of Shouzhou; and more than seventy other generals and officers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Fan Aineng, palace cavalry commander and Kuizhou military governor, He Hui, palace infantry commander and Shouzhou military governor, and more than seventy other officers were executed.

sentences.zh: 高平之役，兩軍既成列，賊騎來挑戰，愛能望風而退，何徽以徒兵陣於後，為奔騎所突，即時潰亂，二將南走。

translations.literal: In the battle of Gaoping, after the two armies had formed their lines, rebel cavalry came to challenge; Aineng fled at the sight of the wind; He Hui had foot soldiers drawn up in the rear, and when fleeing cavalry burst through them they immediately collapsed in disorder; the two generals fled south.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoping, once the armies were drawn up, enemy cavalry rode out to challenge. Fan Aineng fled at the first contact. He Hui had placed his infantry in the rear; fleeing horsemen crashed through them and the line broke instantly. Both generals fled south.

sentences.zh: 帝遣近臣宣諭止遏，莫肯從命，皆揚言曰：「官軍大敗，餘眾已解甲矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent close attendants to proclaim orders to halt and restrain them, but none would obey; all shouted aloud: "The imperial army has suffered a great defeat; the remaining troops have already cast off their armor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent close attendants to order them to stop, but they refused and shouted that the imperial army had been routed and the survivors had already thrown down their arms.

sentences.zh: 」至暮，以官軍克捷，方稍稍而回。

translations.literal: " Only at dusk, when the imperial army had won victory, did they slowly turn back.
translations.idiomatic: " Only at dusk, when news of victory reached them, did they drift slowly back.

sentences.zh: 帝至潞州，錄其奔遁者，自軍使以上及監押使臣並斬之，由是驕將墮兵，無不知懼。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Luzhou, he recorded those who had fled; from army commissioners upward and supervising commissioners, all were beheaded; from this arrogant generals and lax soldiers all knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou he listed every officer who had fled and executed every army commissioner, supervisor, and commissary involved. From that day arrogant commanders and slack troops alike learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 帝以何徽有平陽守禦之功，欲貸其罪，竟不可，與愛能俱殺之，皆給槥車歸葬。

translations.literal: Because He Hui had merit in defending and holding Pingyang, the Emperor wished to spare his punishment, but ultimately could not; together with Aineng he killed them, and both were provided coffin carts to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to spare He Hui because of his service defending Pingyang, but could not; he was executed together with Fan Aineng, and both were sent home in coffin carts for burial.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《東都事略》：世宗謂張永德曰：「樊愛能及偏裨七十餘人，吾欲盡按軍法，何如？

translations.literal: (The 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》 says: Shizong said to Zhang Yongde: "Fan Aineng and more than seventy junior officers—I wish to punish them all according to military law; what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》: Shizong said to Zhang Yongde, "Fan Aineng and more than seventy junior officers—I want to punish them all under military law. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「必欲開拓疆宇，威加四海，安可已也！

translations.literal: " He replied: "If you must expand the realm and extend awe over the four seas, how can you stop!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "If you mean to expand the realm and awe the four seas, how can you stop now!

sentences.zh: 」世宗善其言，悉誅愛能等以徇，軍聲始振。）〉

translations.literal: " Shizong approved his words; he put Aineng and the others to death as a warning, and the army's spirit was first aroused.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong approved his counsel, executed Fan Aineng and the rest as a warning, and the army's morale was roused for the first time.)〉

sentences.zh: 庚子，以侍衛馬步都虞候李重進為許州節度使，以宣徽南院使向訓為滑州節度使，以殿前都指揮使張永德為武信軍節度使，職並如故。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Li Chongjin, chief of staff for palace horse and foot, was made military governor of Xuzhou; Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military governor of Huazhou; Zhang Yongde, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was made military governor of the Wuxin Army—their posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Li Chongjin, palace horse-and-foot chief of staff, took Xuzhou; Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun took Huazhou; and Palace Front commander Zhang Yongde took the Wuxin Army—all retaining their existing posts.

sentences.zh: 以滑州節度使白重贊為鄜州節度使，以鄭州防禦使史彥超為華州節度使，賞高平之功也。

translations.literal: Bai Chongzan, military governor of Huazhou, was made military governor of Yongzhou; Shi Yanchao, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was made military governor of Hua Prefecture, in reward for merit at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou's Bai Chongzan was moved to Yongzhou and Zhengzhou's Shi Yanchao to Hua Prefecture, rewarding their service at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 以晉州節度使藥元福為同州節度使，以宣徽北院使楊廷璋為晉州節度使，以同州節度使張鐸為彰義軍節度使，以客省使吳延祚為宣徽北院使，以龍捷左廂都指揮使李千為蔡州防禦使，以龍捷右廂都指揮使田中為密州防禦使，以虎捷右廂都指揮使張順為登州防禦使，以龍捷左第二軍都指揮使孫延進為鄭州防禦使，以前耀州團練使符彥能為澤州防禦使，以散員都指揮使李繼勛為殿前都虞候，以殿前都虞候韓令坤為龍捷左廂都指揮使，以鐵騎第一軍都指揮使趙宏殷為龍捷右廂都指揮使，以散員都指揮使慕容延釗為虎捷左廂都指揮使，以控鶴第一軍都指揮使趙鼎為虎捷右廂都指揮使，並遙授團練使，其餘改轉有差。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu, military governor of Jinzhou, was made military governor of Tongzhou; Yang Tingzhang, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military governor of Jinzhou; Zhang Duo, military governor of Tongzhou, was made military governor of the Zhangyi Army; Wu Yanzuo, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat; Li Qian, commander of the left wing of the Longjie Army, was made defense commissioner of Caizhou; Tian Zhong, commander of the right wing of the Longjie Army, was made defense commissioner of Mizhou; Zhang Shun, commander of the right wing of the Hujie Army, was made defense commissioner of Dengzhou; Sun Yanjin, commander of the second army of the Longjie left wing, was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou; Fu Yanneng, former regimental trainer of Yaozhou, was made defense commissioner of Zezhou; Li Jixun, commander of the Loose Retainers, was made chief of staff of the Palace Front Division; Han Lingkun, chief of staff of the Palace Front Division, was made commander of the left wing of the Longjie Army; Zhao Hongyin, commander of the first army of the Iron Cavalry, was made commander of the right wing of the Longjie Army; Murong Yanzhao, commander of the Loose Retainers, was made commander of the left wing of the Hujie Army; Zhao Ding, commander of the first army of the Red-crane Guards, was made commander of the right wing of the Hujie Army—all were given concurrent appointment as regimental trainer at a distance, while others were promoted or transferred in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou's Yao Yuanfu took Tongzhou; Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner Yang Tingzhang took Jinzhou; Tongzhou's Zhang Duo took the Zhangyi Army; reception commissioner Wu Yanzuo became Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner; Longjie left commander Li Qian took Caizhou; Longjie right commander Tian Zhong took Mizhou; Hujie right commander Zhang Shun took Dengzhou; Longjie second-left commander Sun Yanjin took Zhengzhou; former Yaozhou trainer Fu Yanneng took Zezhou; Loose Retainers commander Li Jixun became Palace Front chief of staff; Palace Front chief Han Lingkun took the Longjie left wing; Iron Cavalry first-army commander Zhao Hongyin took the Longjie right wing; Loose Retainers commander Murong Yanzhao took the Hujie left wing; and Red-crane first-army commander Zhao Ding took the Hujie right wing—all received distant regimental-trainer titles, while other promotions and transfers varied.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以天雄軍節度使、衛王符彥卿為河東行營都部署，知太原行府事；

translations.literal: On renyin, Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei, was made overall deployer of the Hedong campaign headquarters and acting administrator of the Taiyuan field headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Tianxiong military governor and Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was made overall deployer of the Hedong campaign and acting administrator of the Taiyuan field headquarters;

sentences.zh: 以澶州節度使郭崇為行營副部署；

translations.literal: Guo Chong, military governor of Cangzhou, was made deputy deployer of the campaign headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou's Guo Chong was made deputy deployer;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使向訓為行營兵馬都監；

translations.literal: Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made overseer of campaign horse and foot;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun was made overseer of campaign forces;

sentences.zh: 以侍衛都虞候李重進為行營都虞候。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin, chief of staff of the palace guard, was made chief of staff of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard chief of staff Li Chongjin was made campaign chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 以華州節度使史彥超為先鋒都指揮使，領步騎二萬，進討河東。

translations.literal: Shi Yanchao, military governor of Hua Prefecture, was made overall commander of the vanguard, leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to advance and attack Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Prefecture military governor Shi Yanchao was named vanguard commander and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against Hedong.

sentences.zh: 詔河中節度使王彥超、陜府節度使韓通，率兵自陰地關討賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Yanchao, military governor of Hezhong, and Han Tong, military governor of Shaanfu, to lead troops from Yindi Pass to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong's Wang Yanchao and Shaanfu's Han Tong were ordered to lead troops through Yindi Pass against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以河陽節度使劉詞為隨駕都部署，以鄜州節度使白重贊為隨駕副部署。

translations.literal: Liu Ci, military governor of Heyang, was made deployer accompanying the imperial carriage; Bai Chongzan, military governor of Yongzhou, was made deputy deployer accompanying the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang's Liu Ci was made deployer accompanying the imperial carriage, with Yongzhou's Bai Chongzan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙巳，太祖靈駕發東京。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on yisi, the spirit carriage of Taizu departed from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yisi, Taizu's spirit carriage departed the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，葬於嵩陵。

translations.literal: On yimao, he was buried at Song Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he was buried at Song Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王彥超奏，偽汾州防禦使董希顏以城歸順。

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao, military governor of Hezhong, memorialized that Dong Xiyan, pseudo defense commissioner of Fenzhou, had surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong military governor Wang Yanchao reported that pseudo Fenzhou defense commissioner Dong Xiyan had surrendered the city.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王彥超傳》：彥超自陰地關與符彥卿會兵圍汾州，諸將請急攻，彥超曰：「城已危矣，旦暮將降，我士卒精銳，驅以先登，必死傷者眾，少待之。

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Wang Yanchao》 in the 《History of Song》: Yanchao from Yindi Pass joined Fu Yanqing to surround Fenzhou; the generals requested a rapid assault; Yanchao said: "The city is already in peril and will surrender before long; our troops are elite and keen—if we drive them to be first over the wall, many must be killed and wounded; wait a little."
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《History of Song》 biography of Wang Yanchao: from Yindi Pass he joined Fu Yanqing to besiege Fenzhou. The generals urged a rapid assault, but Yanchao said, "The city is already desperate and will surrender soon. Our men are elite—if we drive them to scale the walls first, casualties will be heavy. Wait a little.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，州將董希顏果降。）〉

translations.literal: " The next day, the prefectural commander Dong Xiyan indeed surrendered.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " The next day prefectural commander Dong Xiyan did surrender.)〉

sentences.zh: 丙辰，偽遼州刺史張漢超以城歸順。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Zhang Hanchao, pseudo prefect of Liaozhou, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen pseudo Liaozhou prefect Zhang Hanchao surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，幸柏谷寺。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Emperor visited Boggu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor visited Boggu Temple.

sentences.zh: 遣右僕射、平章事、判三司李穀赴河東城下，計度軍儲。

translations.literal: He dispatched Li Gu, Right Vice Director, Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions, to the walls of Hedong to plan army supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Right Vice Director and councilor Li Gu, who also headed the Three Fiscal Commissions, to the Hedong front to plan army supplies.

sentences.zh: 詔河東城下諸將，招撫戶口，禁止侵掠，只令征納當年租稅，及募民入粟五百斛、草五百圍者賜出身，千斛、千圍者授州縣官。

translations.literal: An edict to the generals below the walls of Hedong ordered them to pacify and register households, forbid plunder, levy only that year's rents and taxes, grant commoner status to those who contributed five hundred hu of grain or five hundred bundles of fodder, and appoint to prefectural or county office those who contributed one thousand hu or one thousand bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Generals at the Hedong front were ordered to register and pacify the populace, forbid looting, and collect only that year's rents and taxes. Commoners who contributed five hundred hu of grain or five hundred bundles of fodder would receive commoner-official status; those who gave one thousand hu or one thousand bundles would receive prefectural or county appointments.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，符彥卿奏，嵐、憲二州歸順。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Fu Yanqing memorialized that Lan and Xian prefectures had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Fu Yanqing reported that Lan and Xian prefectures had submitted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，制立衛國夫人符氏為皇后，仍令有司擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: On renxu, by imperial order the Lady Fu of the State of Wei was established as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Lady Fu of Wei was formally made empress, with orders to the responsible offices to choose a day and prepare the investiture rites.

sentences.zh: 王彥超奏，收下石州，獲偽刺史安彥進。

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao memorialized that he had taken Shizhou and captured the pseudo prefect An Yanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao reported that he had taken Shizhou and captured pseudo prefect An Yanjin.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王彥超傳》：引兵趣石州，彥超親鼓士乘城，躬冒矢石，數日下之，擒其守將安彥進獻行在。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Wang Yanchao》 in the 《History of Song》: Leading troops toward Shizhou, Yanchao himself beat the drum as soldiers assaulted the walls, personally braving arrows and stones; within several days he took it, seized its defending commander An Yanjin, and presented him at the imperial encampment.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《History of Song》 biography of Wang Yanchao: marching on Shizhou, he personally beat the drum as his men scaled the walls and braved arrows and stones himself. Within days the city fell; he seized defending commander An Yanjin and presented him at the imperial camp.)〉

sentences.zh: 癸亥，偽沁州刺史李廷誨以城歸順。

translations.literal: On guihai, Li Tinghui, pseudo prefect of Qinzhou, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai pseudo Qinzhou prefect Li Tinghui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 甲子，皇妹壽安公主張氏進封晉國長公主。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Emperor's younger sister, the Princess of Shou'an, née Zhang, was advanced to Grand Princess of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor's younger sister, Princess Shou'an of the Zhang clan, was advanced to Grand Princess of Jin.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，東京奏，太師、中書令馮道薨。

translations.literal: On yichou, a memorial from the Eastern Capital reported that Grand Preceptor and Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery Feng Dao had died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Eastern Capital reported that Grand Preceptor and councilor Feng Dao had died.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，太祖皇帝神主祔於太廟。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the spirit tablet of Emperor Taizu was installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet was installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 庚午，曲赦潞州見禁罪人，除死罪外並釋放。

translations.literal: On gengwu, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for prisoners held in Luzhou; all except those guilty of capital crimes were released.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu a partial amnesty was proclaimed for prisoners in Luzhou; all except those sentenced to death were released.

sentences.zh: 是日，車駕發潞州，親征劉崇。

translations.literal: That day the imperial carriage departed Luzhou to campaign in person against Liu Chong.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor left Luzhou to campaign in person against Liu Chong.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，忻州偽監軍李殺刺史趙臯及契丹大將楊耨姑，以州城歸順。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Li, pseudo overseer of the army at Xinzhou, killed the prefect Zhao Gao and the Khitan grand general Yang Nuogu, and surrendered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou pseudo Xinzhou army overseer Li killed prefect Zhao Gao and the Khitan grand general Yang Nuogu and surrendered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔授李忻州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li military governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li military governor of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，以尚書右丞邊歸讜守本官，充樞密直學士；

translations.literal: Fifth month, yihai, Bian Guidan was ordered to remain in his original post of Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was appointed direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yihai, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Bian Guidan kept his post and was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以尚書戶部侍郎陶穀守本官，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Tao Gu, Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue, was ordered to remain in his original post and was appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Tao Gu kept his post and was made Hanlin academician.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·陶穀傳》：從征太原，時魚崇諒迎母後至，穀乘間言曰：「崇諒宿留不來，有顧望意。

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Tao Gu》 in the 《History of Song》: During the campaign against Taiyuan, when Yu Chongliang was escorting his mother and she arrived behind, Gu seized an opportunity to say: "Chongliang's prolonged stay and failure to come—he harbors thoughts of hesitation."
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《History of Song》 biography of Tao Gu: on the Taiyuan campaign, when Yu Chongliang was escorting his mother and she arrived later, Gu seized a moment to say, "Chongliang has lingered and not come forward—he is hesitating."

sentences.zh: 」世宗頗疑之。

translations.literal: " Shizong was quite suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong grew quite suspicious.

sentences.zh: 崇諒又表陳母病，詔許歸陜州就養，以穀為翰林學士。）〉

translations.literal: Chongliang again memorialized that his mother was ill; an edict permitted him to return to Shaanzhou to support her, and Gu was made Hanlin academician.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang then memorialized that his mother was ill; an edict let him return to Shaanzhou to care for her, and Gu was made Hanlin academician.)〉

sentences.zh: 丙子，車駕至太原城下。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the imperial carriage reached below the walls of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor reached the walls of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 是日，偽代州防禦使鄭處謙以城歸順。

translations.literal: That day, Zheng Chuqian, pseudo defense commissioner of Daizhou, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: That day pseudo Daizhou defense commissioner Zheng Chuqian surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，觀兵於太原城下，帝親自慰勉，錫賚有差。

translations.literal: On dingchou, he reviewed the troops below the walls of Taiyuan; the Emperor personally comforted and encouraged them, with rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he reviewed the troops below Taiyuan; the emperor personally encouraged them and gave rewards in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 升代州為節鎮，以靜塞軍為額，以鄭處謙為節度使。

translations.literal: Daizhou was elevated to a military commission, with the designation Jingsai Army; Zheng Chuqian was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Daizhou was elevated to a military commission under the name Jingsai Army, and Zheng Chuqian was made its military governor.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，斬偽命石州刺史安彥進於太原城下，以其拒王師也。

translations.literal: On wuyin, An Yanjin, pseudo prefect of Shizhou by rebel appointment, was beheaded below the walls of Taiyuan, because he had resisted the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin An Yanjin, the rebel-appointed prefect of Shizhou, was beheaded below Taiyuan for resisting the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以前忠武軍節度使郭從義為天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Guo Congyi, former military governor of the Zhongwu Army, was made military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen former Zhongwu military governor Guo Congyi was made Tianping military governor.

sentences.zh: 遣符彥卿、郭從義、向訓、白重贊、史彥超等，率步騎萬餘赴忻州。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing, Guo Congyi, Xiang Xun, Bai Chongzan, Shi Yanchao, and others were dispatched to lead more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to proceed to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, Guo Congyi, Xiang Xun, Bai Chongzan, Shi Yanchao, and others were sent with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to Xinzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《宋史·符彥卿傳》：彥卿之行也，世宗以並人雖敗，朝廷饋運不繼，未議攻擊，且令觀兵城下，徐圖進取。

translations.literal: (The 《Biography of Fu Yanqing》 in the 《History of Song》: On Yanqing's march, Shizong held that although the Bing men had been defeated, the court's supply transport did not continue, and no assault was yet discussed; he only ordered a review of troops below the walls and a gradual plan for advance.
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《History of Song》 biography of Fu Yanqing: when Yanqing marched, Shizong held that although the Bingzhou forces had been beaten, court supply lines were not keeping up and no assault was yet planned; he ordered only a show of force below the walls while advancing gradually.

sentences.zh: 及周師入境，汾、晉吏民望風款接，皆以久罹虐政，願輸軍需以資兵力。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army entered the territory, officials and people of Fen and Jin received them with submission at the sight of the wind; all, having long suffered harsh government, wished to supply military needs to support the army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou troops entered the region, officials and people of Fen and Jin submitted at the first approach; having long suffered harsh rule, they offered supplies to support the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗從之，而連下數州。

translations.literal: Shizong followed this, and in succession several prefectures were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong accepted this, and several prefectures fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 彥卿等皆以芻糧未備，欲旋軍，世宗不之省，乃調山東近郡免軍食濟之。）〉

translations.literal: Yanqing and the others all held that fodder and grain were not prepared and wished to withdraw the army; Shizong did not heed this and instead levied the nearby prefectures of Shandong, exempting them from military grain levies to supply them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing and the others all said fodder and grain were not ready and wanted to withdraw, but Shizong ignored them and instead drew supplies from nearby Shandong prefectures by exempting them from military grain levies.)〉

sentences.zh: 是夜大風，發屋拔樹。

translations.literal: That night a great wind arose, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees.
translations.idiomatic: That night a great wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以宰臣李穀判太原行府事。

translations.literal: On renwu, Li Gu the chief minister was assigned to administer the Taiyuan field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu chief minister Li Gu was assigned to administer the Taiyuan field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，升府州為節鎮，以永安軍為軍額，以本州防禦使折德扆為節度使。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Fuzhou was elevated to a military commission, with the designation Yong'an Army; She Dedeyi, defense commissioner of that prefecture, was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Fuzhou was elevated to a military commission under the name Yong'an Army, and its defense commissioner She Dedeyi was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯朔，詔班師，車駕發離太原。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guimao new moon, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army; the imperial carriage departed from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon of the sixth month an edict ordered withdrawal; the emperor left Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時大集兵賦，及征山東、懷、孟、蒲、陜丁夫數萬，急攻其城，旦夕之間，期於必取。

translations.literal: At the time they had mustered troops and levies on a great scale, and conscripted tens of thousands of laborers from Shandong, Huai, Meng, Pu, and Shaan to assault the city urgently; within a mere day or two they expected certain capture.
translations.idiomatic: They had mustered troops and levies on a vast scale and conscripted tens of thousands of laborers from Shandong, Huai, Meng, Pu, and Shaan for an urgent assault, expecting the city to fall within a day or two.

sentences.zh: 會大雨時行，軍士勞苦，復以忻口之師不振，帝遂決旋師之意。

translations.literal: But continuous heavy rains fell, the troops suffered hardship, and because the army at Xinkou had not prospered, the Emperor thereupon resolved to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: But heavy rains persisted, the troops were exhausted, and because the force at Xinkou had not prospered, the emperor resolved to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 指麾之間，頗傷匆遽，部伍紛亂，無復嚴整，不逞之徒訛言相恐，隨軍資用頗有遺失者，賊城之下，糧草數十萬，悉焚棄之。

translations.literal: In directing the withdrawal it was rather hasty and damaging; ranks fell into disorder and were no longer strict; mischief-makers spread frightening rumors; a fair amount of military supplies was lost along the march; below the rebel walls several hundred thousand units of grain and fodder were all burned and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The withdrawal was managed in haste; ranks broke up and discipline collapsed. Troublemakers spread alarming rumors, and much equipment was lost on the march. Below the rebel walls several hundred thousand units of grain and fodder were burned and abandoned.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引《晉陽見聞錄》：六月旦，周師南轅返騑，惟數百騎，間之以步卒千人，長槍赤甲，衒趫捷跳梁於城隅，晡晚殺行而抽退。

translations.literal: (The 《Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Records of What Was Seen at Jinyang》: On the first of the sixth month the Zhou army turned its chariots south and returned; only several hundred cavalry, interspersed with a thousand foot soldiers with long spears and red armor, displayed agility and leapt about at the corners of the wall; toward late afternoon they slowed the march and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Records of What Was Seen at Jinyang》: on the first of the sixth month the Zhou army turned south with only a few hundred cavalry, interspersed with a thousand foot soldiers in red armor with long spears who displayed agility and leapt about at the wall corners; toward late afternoon they slowed the march and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 《宋史·藥元福傳》：詔令班師，元福上言曰：「進軍甚易，退軍甚難。

translations.literal: The 《Biography of Yao Yuanfu》 in the 《History of Song》: When an edict ordered withdrawal, Yuanfu memorialized, saying, "Advancing the army is very easy; withdrawing the army is very difficult."
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Song》 biography of Yao Yuanfu records that when an edict ordered withdrawal, Yuanfu memorialized, "Advancing is easy; withdrawing is hard."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「一以委卿。

translations.literal: " Shizong said: "I leave it all to you."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong said, "I leave it entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 」遂部分卒伍為方陣而南，元福以麾下為後殿。

translations.literal: " He thereupon arrayed the soldiers in square formation facing south; Yuanfu with his command served as the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He then arrayed the troops in square formations facing south, with Yuanfu and his command as the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 崇果出兵來追，元福擊走之。）〉

translations.literal: Liu Chong indeed sent troops in pursuit; Yuanfu struck and drove them off.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong did send troops in pursuit, but Yuanfu struck and drove them off.)〉

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車駕至潞州。

translations.literal: On yisi, the imperial carriage reached Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the emperor reached Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝發潞州。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Emperor departed Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the emperor left Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，幸新鄭縣。

translations.literal: On yichou, he visited Xinzheng County.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he visited Xinzheng County.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，帝親拜嵩陵，祭奠而退。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Emperor personally paid obeisance at Song Mausoleum, offered sacrifice, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the emperor personally paid obeisance at Song Mausoleum, offered sacrifice, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賜守陵將吏及近陵戶帛有差。

translations.literal: The generals, officials, and households near the mausoleum who guarded it were granted silk in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb guardians, officials, and nearby households were granted silk in varying measure.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：顯德元年二月，車駕征太原回，親拜嵩陵，望陵號慟。

translations.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials》: In the second month of Xiande year 1, as the imperial carriage returned from the campaign against Taiyuan, he personally paid obeisance at Song Mausoleum, gazed at the tomb and wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials》 records that in the second month of Xiande 1, returning from the Taiyuan campaign, he personally paid obeisance at Song Mausoleum, gazed at the tomb, and wailed in grief.

sentences.zh: 至陵所，俯伏哀泣，感於左右，再拜訖，祭奠而退。）〉

translations.literal: Reaching the tomb site, he prostrated himself and wept in grief, moving those at his side; when the second obeisance was finished, he offered sacrifice and withdrew.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At the tomb he prostrated himself and wept, moving those around him; after a second obeisance he offered sacrifice and withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝至自河東。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Emperor returned from Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor returned from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉朔，前河西軍節度使申師厚責授右監門衛率府副率。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, guiyou new moon, Shen Shihou, former military governor of the Hexi Army, was demoted and appointed Vice Leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou new moon of the seventh month of autumn, former Hexi military governor Shen Shihou was demoted to vice leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.

sentences.zh: 師厚在涼州歲餘，以所部艱食，蕃情反覆，奏乞入朝，尋留其子為留後，不俟詔離任，故責之。

translations.literal: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year; because his command lacked food and the tribal disposition was inconstant, he memorialized begging to enter court; soon he left his son as acting commissioner without awaiting an edict and left his post—hence the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year. His troops lacked food and the tribes were unreliable, so he memorialized asking to come to court. He soon left his son as acting commissioner, left his post without awaiting an edict, and was punished for it.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，天雄軍節度使、衛王府彥卿進位守太傅，改封魏王；

translations.literal: On yihai, Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei, was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Tianxiong military governor and Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;

sentences.zh: 鄆州郭從義加兼中書令；

translations.literal: Guo Congyi of Yanzhou was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou's Guo Congyi was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 河陽劉詞移鎮永興軍，加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Liu Ci of Heyang was transferred to the Yongxing Army and additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Heyang's Liu Ci was transferred to Yongxing and additionally made palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 潞州李筠加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Li Jun of Luzhou was additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's Li Jun was additionally made palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 河中王彥超移鎮許州，加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong's Wang Yanchao was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 許州節度、侍衛都虞候李重進移鎮宋州，加同平章事兼侍衛親軍都指揮使；

translations.literal: Li Chongjin, military governor of Xuzhou and chief of staff of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, made concurrent Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou military governor and palace guard chief of staff Li Chongjin was transferred to Songzhou, made councilor, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;

sentences.zh: 以武信軍節度使兼殿前都指揮使張永德為滑州節度使，加檢校太傅，典軍如故；

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde, military governor of the Wuxin Army and commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was made military governor of Huazhou, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and retained command of the army as before;
translations.idiomatic: Wuxin military governor and Palace Front commander Zhang Yongde was made Huazhou military governor, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and kept army command as before;

sentences.zh: 同州藥元福移鎮陜州，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu of Tongzhou was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou's Yao Yuanfu was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

sentences.zh: 鄜州白重贊移鎮河陽，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: Bai Chongzan of Yongzhou was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou's Bai Chongzan was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

sentences.zh: 陜州韓通移鎮曹州，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Han Tong of Shaanzhou was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanzhou's Han Tong was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝即位之初，覃慶於諸侯，是賞從征之功也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Emperor's accession he had bestowed rewards widely upon the feudal lords; this was to reward merit from the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his reign he had extended rewards widely to the feudal lords; this round rewarded those who had joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以前禮部侍郎邊光範為刑部侍郎，權判開封府事。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Bian Guangfan, former Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi former Vice Minister of Rites Bian Guangfan was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，天下兵馬元帥、吳越國王錢俶加天下兵馬都元帥；

translations.literal: On dingchou, Qian Chu, King of Wu-Yue and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven, was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wu-Yue king and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven Qian Chu was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 襄州節度使、陳王安審琦加守太尉。

translations.literal: Wang Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou and Prince of Chen, was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou military governor and Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，右散騎常侍張可復卒。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Zhang Kefu, Right Regular Attendant, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Right Regular Attendant Zhang Kefu died.

sentences.zh: 以前亳州防禦使李萬金為鄜州留後。

translations.literal: Li Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former Bozhou defense commissioner Li Wanjin was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，幸南莊。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor visited the South Manor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor visited the South Manor.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，荊南節度使、南平王高保融加守中書令，夏州節度使、西平王李彜興加守太保，西京留守武行德、徐州王晏、鄧州侯章並加兼中書令。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Gao Baorong, military governor of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping, was advanced to Defender Councilor; Li Yixing, military governor of Xiazhou and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, Wang Yan of Xuzhou, and Hou Zhang of Dengzhou were all additionally made Councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Jingnan military governor and Prince of Nanping Gao Baorong was advanced to Defender Councilor; Xiazhou military governor and Prince of Xiping Li Yixing was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde, Xuzhou's Wang Yan, and Dengzhou's Hou Zhang were all additionally made councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 癸未，湖南王進逵加兼中書令；

translations.literal: On guimao, Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Hunan's Wang Jinkui was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 天德軍節度使郭勛、邠州折從阮、安州李洪義並加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Guo Xun, military governor of the Tiande Army, Zhe Congruan of Binzhou, and Li Hongyi of Anzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Tiande military governor Guo Xun, Binzhou's Zhe Congruan, and Anzhou's Li Hongyi were all additionally made palace attendants;

sentences.zh: 以前華州節度使孫方諫為同州節度使，加兼中書令；

translations.literal: Previously Sun Fangjian, military governor of Hua, was made military governor of Tong, additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: Former Hua military governor Sun Fangjian was appointed military governor of Tong and additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 以前永興軍節度使王仁鎬為河中節度使，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Previously Wang Rengao, military governor of the Yongxing Army, was made military governor of Hezhong, promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yongxing military governor Wang Rengao was appointed military governor of Hezhong and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，滄州李暉、貝州王饒、鎮州曹英並加兼侍中，涇州張鐸、相州王進、延州袁鳷並加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Li Hui of Cangzhou, Wang Rao of Beizhou, and Cao Ying of Zhenzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants; Zhang Duo of Jingzhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Yuan Zhi of Yanzhou were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Cangzhou's Li Hui, Beizhou's Wang Rao, and Zhenzhou's Cao Ying were all additionally made palace attendants; Jingzhou's Zhang Duo, Xiangzhou's Wang Jin, and Yanzhou's Yuan Zhi were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，百僚上表，請以九月二十四日誕聖日為天清節，從之。

translations.literal: On renchen, the hundred officials submitted a memorial requesting that the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day of the sage's birth, be established as the Tianqing Festival; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the officials memorialized to make the emperor's birthday, the twenty-fourth of the ninth month, the Tianqing Festival. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史範質為守司徒兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士；

translations.literal: On guisi, Fan Zhi, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, and supervisor of state history Fan Zhi was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《國老談苑》云：周太祖嘗令世宗詣範質，時為親王，軒車高大，門不能容，世宗即下馬步入。

translations.literal: (The 《Guolao Tanyuan》 states: Zhou Taizu once had Shizong go to Fan Zhi's residence; he was then a prince. His carriage was tall and the gate could not admit it; Shizong at once dismounted and walked in on foot.
translations.idiomatic: (The Guolao Tanyuan records that Zhou Taizu once sent Shizong to visit Fan Zhi when the latter was still a prince. Shizong's carriage was so tall the gate would not take it, so he dismounted and entered on foot.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，從容語質曰：「卿所居舊宅耶，門樓一何小哉。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he said to Fan Zhi in an easy manner: "Is this the old residence in which you dwell? How very small the gate-tower is!"
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, he said to Fan Zhi with easy familiarity, "Is this your old house? What a tiny gate-tower!"

sentences.zh: 」遂為治第。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon a mansion was built for him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He then had a new residence built for him.)〉

sentences.zh: 以左僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士、判三司李穀為守司徒兼門下侍朗、平章事，監修國史；

translations.literal: Li Gu, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history;
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices Li Gu was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made supervisor of state history;

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事王溥為中書侍郎兼禮部尚書、平章事、集賢殿大學士；

translations.literal: Wang Pu, Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, was made Secretariat Chamberlain concurrently Minister of Rites, Councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor Wang Pu was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Minister of Rites, councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;

sentences.zh: 以樞密院學士、工部侍郎景範為中書侍郎、平章事，判三司；

translations.literal: Jing Fan, Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works, was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, overseeing the Three Offices;
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works Jing Fan was made Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, with charge of the Three Offices;

sentences.zh: 樞密使、檢校太保、同平章事鄭仁誨加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and Concurrent Councilor, was additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and concurrent councilor Zheng Renhui was additionally made palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 靈武馮繼業、定州孫行友、邢州田景鹹並加檢校太傅；
